# A simulated quadcopter in an underground mine, GNSS denied: it lifts off
# in the level station, turns 180 degrees and flies west down a 5 m wide
# drift with rough rock walls, speeding up to 8 m/s between 1 and 2.5 m
# above the floor: 10.7 s, 30 m. A planar LiDAR (500 beams, 10 Hz, 12 m)
# sees the drift walls through dust. A downward optical-flow sensor and
# rangefinder on the flight controller measure the ground velocity.
# Lines in time order:
#   g t_us wx wy wz ax ay az     a 100 Hz IMU: body rate (FLU, microrad/s)
#                                and specific force (mm/s²)
#   v t_us vx vy                 the flight controller's OPTICAL_FLOW rates
#                                (compensated for the body rate) times its
#                                downward rangefinder's range: the body
#                                velocity along x and y (FLU), mm/s
#   s t_us x y yaw n (dk r)*n    one revolution starting at t_us: its true
#                                position (mm, z-up world, from the first
#                                revolution) and yaw (microradians), then n
#                                returns as the beam slot step from the
#                                previous return (slot k fires k/500 of the
#                                period after t_us, at azimuth k·0.72
#                                degrees counter-clockwise from +x) and the
#                                range in mm
